claims.claim: The Tow Center found that premium chatbots gave more confidently incorrect answers than their free counterparts.
claims.source: Jazwinska and Chandrasekar, Tow Center for Digital Journalism, Columbia Journalism Review, 6 March 2025
claims.quote: Premium chatbots provided more confidently incorrect answers than their free counterparts

claims.claim: The Tow Center's task was explicitly archival: the tools were asked for an article's headline, original publisher, publication date and URL.
claims.source: Jazwinska and Chandrasekar, Tow Center for Digital Journalism, Columbia Journalism Review, 6 March 2025
claims.quote: headline, original publisher, publication date, and URL

claims.claim: On the 2026 ProHist-Bench of professional historical research tasks the authors report that the tasks remain extremely difficult for all current models.
claims.source: Lirong Gao, Zeqing Wang, Yuyan Cai, Jiayi Deng, Yanmei Gu, Yiming Zhang, Jia Zhou, Yanfei Zhang and Junbo Zhao (Zhejiang University and Ant Group), 'Can LLMs Act as Historians? ProHist-Bench', arXiv 2604.24690v1, 27 April 2026
claims.quote: remain extremely difficult for all current LLMs

claims.claim: GPT-5.2 recorded a Rubric Score of 11.07 on ProHist-Bench, below several smaller and open models on the same table.
claims.source: Gao, Wang, Cai, Deng et al., 'Can LLMs Act as Historians? ProHist-Bench', arXiv 2604.24690v1, 27 April 2026

claims.claim: ProHist-Bench scores 400 expert-curated questions spanning eight dynasties against 10,891 fine-grained rubrics.
claims.source: Gao, Wang, Cai, Deng et al., 'Can LLMs Act as Historians? ProHist-Bench', arXiv 2604.24690v1, 27 April 2026

claims.claim: Qwen3-Max achieved the strongest overall Bonus Score performance on ProHist-Bench, ahead of the Western frontier models tested.
claims.source: Gao, Wang, Cai, Deng et al., 'Can LLMs Act as Historians? ProHist-Bench', arXiv 2604.24690v1, 27 April 2026
claims.quote: Qwen3-Max achieves the strongest overall performance

claims.claim: English Wikipedia's speedy-deletion criterion G15 applies only to a page exhibiting one of three named signs that indicate the page could only plausibly have been generated by a large language model.
claims.source: English Wikipedia policy page 'Criteria for speedy deletion', criterion G15 (community-adopted policy text)
claims.quote: exhibits any of the three following signs which indicate that the page

claims.claim: The G15 criterion states that the more subjective signs of LLM writing must not be the sole basis for applying the criterion.
claims.source: English Wikipedia policy page 'Criteria for speedy deletion', criterion G15
claims.quote: which should not serve as the sole basis for applying this criterion
claims.page: G15. Unambiguously LLM-generated pages, closing paragraph

claims.claim: The first of G15's three enforceable signs is communication addressed to the user, such as a collaborative preamble, a knowledge-cutoff disclaimer, self-insertion, or an unfilled placeholder.
claims.source: English Wikipedia policy page 'Criteria for speedy deletion', criterion G15, first bullet

claims.claim: G15 instructs a tagging editor not to treat a single bad reference as definitive evidence of LLM generation.
claims.source: English Wikipedia policy page 'Criteria for speedy deletion', criterion G15, second bullet
claims.quote: and not take a single example as definitive
